title: The Lymphatic System as a Modulator of Lipedema: A Clinical and Translational Study of Lymphatic Alterations and Their Pathophysiological Significance
summary:
Lipedema is a chronic condition involving a disproportionate buildup of fat beneath the skin, mainly in the legs and sometimes in the arms. Women affected by lipedema often experience pain, tenderness, and easy bruising. Why symptoms vary in severity between individuals is not yet fully understood. The lymphatic system drains fluid from body tissues. This study will investigate the significance of changes in this system in women with lipedema. Lipedema and lymphedema are considered separate conditions that can occur together.

The study will examine how frequently abnormal lymphatic drainage patterns occur in women with lipedema and whether these patterns are associated with pain, difficulties in daily activities, quality of life, leg circumference, or tissue properties.

At least 80 adult women will be enrolled at BG University Hospital Bergmannsheil Bochum, Germany. At the start of the study, findings from medical examinations and images of the lymphatic vessels obtained during routine care will be evaluated. Participants will complete questionnaires about their symptoms and quality of life. Body measurements, leg volume, and skin elasticity will also be assessed, and a blood sample will be collected. For participants undergoing liposuction as part of their treatment, independently of the study, a small sample of skin and fat tissue will be collected during surgery.

Participants receiving non-surgical treatment will be assessed once, at the start of the study. Participants undergoing surgery will also be assessed during routine follow-up appointments for up to six months after surgery, or up to twelve months if they also have lymphedema. The study does not determine which treatment participants receive. The findings are intended to improve understanding of the different ways lipedema presents and provide a basis for future research.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Female sex.
- Age ≥18 years at enrollment.
- Clinically confirmed lipedema according to the diagnostic criteria of the S2k guideline.
- Attendance at the specialized lipedema and lymphedema outpatient clinic.
- Clinically indicated ICG lymphangiography of the extremities performed as part of routine care.
- Capacity to provide informed consent and provision of written informed consent.
- Sufficient language proficiency.
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
- Active malignancy or a history of malignancy involving the lymphatic system, particularly following lymphadenectomy or radiotherapy involving the extremities.
- Active infection.
- Secondary lymphedema of known etiology.
- Clinically significant chronic venous insufficiency, classified as CEAP clinical class C4 or higher.
- Pre-existing medical conditions that limit study participation.
- Inability to provide informed consent or legal guardianship subject to a consent reservation.
- Known hypersensitivity to indocyanine green, sodium iodide, iodine, or gadolinium-based contrast agents.
- For MRI: claustrophobia or the presence of implants that are not compatible with MRI.
